title: ADAT
summary: ADAT is a magnetic tape format introduced by Alesis in 1991 that records eight digital audio tracks onto standard S-VHS videotape. It enabled affordable multitrack recording for project studios, with units capable of linking together to record up to 128 tracks simultaneously. The format supports 16-bit (Type I) or 20-bit (Type II) samples and offers variable sample rates (44.1 or 48 kHz) for pitch control. Remote operation is possible via dedicated controllers.

mechanisms.title: Tape-based multitrack recording
mechanisms.explanation: ADAT records eight digital audio tracks simultaneously onto an S-VHS videotape using a rotating head and helical scan write method. Multiple ADAT units can be linked together to achieve sample-accurate timing for recording up to 128 tracks at once.

mechanisms.title: Sample-rate pitch control
mechanisms.explanation: Pitch control is achieved by varying the sample rate, which adjusts the tape speed accordingly. The format supports common industry sample rates of 44.1 kHz and 48 kHz, allowing flexibility in recording speed and pitch.
